speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help me narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been present, and did they start suddenly or develop gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of diabetes, anabolic steroid use, and recent significant weight loss, I need to rule out serious metabolic or neoplastic causes. Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or pain in that arm, and do you have any history of tumors or lymph nodes in your neck? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor).

Given your significant weight loss, chronic alcohol use, and steroid history, I am concerned about a malignancy compressing your brachial plexus. I need to visualize the apical region of your right lung. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
